_note: v4 (first trained model: compositional prompt learning on frozen CLIP). Builds on v3's zero-shot prompt (cleaned names + symptom descriptions, HM 10.2%). New: each crop (55) and each disease (175) becomes ONE learnable word vector inside the prompt 'a photo of [CROP] leaves with [DISEASE]: <description>.', initialised from CLIP's embedding of the v2/v3 name. Both CLIP encoders stay frozen; only 230 x 512 = 118k numbers are trained, so overfitting risk is low despite a median of 7 images per pair. Unseen pairs reuse vectors trained on other pairs. Seen-class calibration (gamma) is introduced here: training on seen pairs biases scores towards them, and gamma is chosen on a validation split with pseudo-unseen pairs, never on test.
_result: Big step up from zero-shot. With gamma 0.045 (chosen on validation): harmonic mean 43.6% top-1 / 84.7% top-5 (v3: 10.2% / 30.0%); seen top-1 30.1% / top-5 74.7%, unseen top-1 79.1% / top-5 97.7%. Uncalibrated (gamma 0): HM 34.9%, seen 50.8%, unseen 26.6%; crop correct 83% seen / 70% unseen, disease 55% / 31%. Learning the 230 vectors fixed the disease gap seen in v1-v3. Selection picked epoch 3 of 40: validation pseudo-unseen accuracy peaks at epochs 1-3 and then falls (39% -> 15%) while val-seen keeps rising, so longer training overfits the vectors to the seen pairs; val HM is also noisy epoch to epoch (35.7% at epoch 3 vs 35.7% at epoch 7). Calibration overshoots on test: gamma 0.045 sends 53% of seen-test images to unseen pairs and halves seen top-1 (50.8% -> 30.1%). A diagnostic sweep on test (NOT usable for selection) shows HM would peak near gamma 0.02 (~52.7%), so the validation split mis-estimates gamma. Likely causes: validation ranks against 30 untrained pairs (20 pseudo-unseen + the 10 real unseen) versus 10 at test, and pseudo-unseen is dominated by cassava_mosaic (544 of 1,340 images). Per unseen pair at the chosen gamma: corn_brown_spot and mango_anthracnose 100%, grape_black_rot 85%, tomato_early_blight 82%, pepper_bell_bacterial_spot 73%, cherry_aphis_spp 42% (lowest). Next (v5): make validation mirror test (exclude the real unseen pairs from the validation label space, cap images per pseudo-unseen pair) so gamma transfers, and lower the learning rate so the best epoch is less noisy.

data._note: Trains on DPD_Small train only. Test splits scored against all 333 pairs, as in v1-v3.

model._note: Same frozen OpenAI ViT-B/16 as v1-v3, so image embeddings come from the shared cache.

input._note: Checkpoint preprocessing, no augmentation: the image encoder is frozen and its embeddings are cached once. Augmentation would need several cached views per image; a candidate for a later version.

names._note: Same as v2/v3. Here the names only initialise the learnable vectors; training can move them.

prompts._note: One template (v3 averaged five; with learnable vectors, five templates would cost five text passes per step). Healthy uses the same template, so 'healthy' is a learnable disease vector like the others. The crop-only and disease-only prompts feed the auxiliary losses, which keep each vector meaningful on its own: that is what an unseen pair needs.

validation._note: From train: 20 whole seen pairs (each with >= 8 images) held out as pseudo-unseen, chosen so their crop and disease still occur in training (like the real unseen pairs), plus 15% of the remaining images as val-seen. Picks the epoch and gamma (grid 0 to 0.1, step 0.0025, in cosine-similarity units). 'healthy' pairs are not held out: none of the real unseen pairs is healthy, and without this exclusion 6 of the 20 held-out pairs were healthy (corn_healthy alone has 223 images), which would tune gamma on the wrong kind of class.

training._note: AdamW on the 230 vectors only; weight_decay 0 because decay would pull the vectors towards zero rather than towards their name initialisation. logit_scale 100 = CLIP's own temperature. Cosine LR over the run. final_fit 'all_train': after selection, refit on every training image (the held-out pairs are real seen classes in the test set) for the selected epoch count.

evaluation._note: gamma comes from validation (see validation); metrics.json also reports the uncalibrated harmonic mean.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing in the text encoder: 333 + 55 + 175 prompts go through it every step and the 6 GB GPU cannot hold all activations otherwise.
